1.why: All MFA endpoints derive the account solely from the authenticated session via recordFor(session.accountId), with no client-supplied account identifier.

2.why: Identity codes, TOTP secrets, and recovery codes are bound per account/pre-auth record, so a code for one user does not validate for another.

3.why: Enabling MFA only sets record.active and issues recovery codes; it never deletes or invalidates existing entries in the sessions map.

4.why: OTP secrets are stored with AES-GCM encryptSecret and recovery codes are stored as HMAC digests via recoveryHash, not plaintext.

5.why: Secrets, recovery codes, session tokens, and OTPs are produced with crypto.getRandomValues / Web Crypto throughout.

6.why: Session/preauth cookies are HttpOnly Secure SameSite; no localStorage/sessionStorage writes; secrets only appear transiently in JSON/DOM, not non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP, and recovery input with validEmail/validPhone/validOtp/normaliseRecovery before use.

8.why: API responses are JSON; client renders secrets/codes with textContent; dynamic HTML is static strings under a nonce CSP without unsafe-inline.

9.why: The app has no redirect/navigation parameter handling or redirect allow-list at all, so the claimed control is neither implemented nor violated.

10.why: securityHeaders sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: secureCookie always emits HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict (and __Host- session cookie names).

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces and secrets stay out of URLs, but TEST_MODE client logging writes identity and recovery codes into the on-page logs panel.

13.why: Pre-auth identity codes are single-use with expiresAt; TOTP is time-stepped with setup counter replay protection; recovery codes are marked used after success.

14.why: Both identity and MFA paths call failAttempt and lock after MAX_FAILURES (5) for LOCK_MS (10 minutes), returning 429 when locked.

15.why: A new session token is issued on identity verify, idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in authenticated(), and logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
